_comment: The ONE canonical source for Faust's voice-control label contract.
Two consumers are generated from this file, never hand-edited to match
each other: host/Source/VoiceContract.generated.h (the C++ match list
FaustEngine::extractVoiceControls uses) and the GENERATED VOICE CONTRACT
block in llm/prompts/instrument_prompt.txt (what the model is told).
Regenerate both with: python tools/gen_voice_contract.py --write
Zone order and label order within a zone ARE the match order
(FaustEngine::extractVoiceControls: first match per role wins, and a
patch declaring both 'freq' and 'key' binds only the first one found in
this order). Changing either order changes behaviour -- see
tools/gen_voice_contract.py --check, which is wired into
tools/check.sh's full level.
labels[0] in each zone is the PRIMARY spelling: the one
llm/prompts/instrument_prompt.txt teaches the model to write. Every
other entry is an ALTERNATE spelling FaustEngine still recognises (Faust
hand-written test fixtures, the poly-dsp precedent) but the prompt never
mentions -- teaching the model two names for one slot invites it to pick
either inconsistently. 'rawUnits' on an alternate records why the unit
conversion in FaustEngine::noteOn differs for it (freq wants Hz, key the
raw MIDI note; gain wants 0-1, vel/velocity the raw 0-127).
'promptOrder' is separate from 'zones' order on purpose: 'zones' IS the
C++ match order (gate before freq before gain -- changing it changes
extractVoiceControls's behaviour) while 'promptOrder' is only the
pedagogical order the three declarations appear in the prompt (pitch,
then level, then gate), which carries no match semantics and always
did not match the C++ order even before this file existed.

zones.comment: 1 while the key is held, else 0
